correctness.rationale: For atomless \(\mu\), monotonicity gives the exact quantile update \(Q\mapsto T((1-\varepsilon)Q+\varepsilon R)\), so the common resource term cancels in the one-dimensional \(W_1\) formula before applying \(T\). The fixed-point increment equation and \(\tau\le T'\le L\) yield the two-sided Lipschitz comparison of \(Q_*\) with \(R\), with denominators \(1-\tau(1-\varepsilon)\) and \(1-L(1-\varepsilon)\). Integrating those increment bounds cellwise over the lower-rank empirical quantile gives the exact two-sided \(e_N(\rho)\) equilibrium law. The same cellwise comparison gives the affine transient recurrence. Bi-Lipschitz \(R\) makes \(Q_*\) bi-Lipschitz and hence its pushforward absolutely continuous. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

The theorem identifies the exact finite-size statistic that replaces \(1/N\) and sharpens the lower equilibrium constant even in the original homogeneous case, giving information a future analysis of nonuniform resources can directly use.

final_claim: For a one-dimensional monotone repulsive mean-field contraction with a continuous strictly increasing bi-Lipschitz resource quantile \(R\), the self-consistent update is a contraction in quantile coordinates with factor at most \(L(1-\varepsilon)\); its unique nonatomic equilibrium has a bi-Lipschitz quantile, and the ordered \(N\)-particle equilibrium error is trapped between the stated two multiples of the resource quantization error \(e_N(\rho)\), including the strengthened uniform-resource lower constant.
limitations: The resource quantile is assumed continuous, strictly increasing and bi-Lipschitz.
Uniqueness is asserted in the nonatomic quantile class, not among arbitrary atomic invariant measures.
